answer: Agents can require each new account to lock a scarce, transferable token for a fixed period before it may submit work or vote. The protocol caps influence by locked stake, so creating a thousand identities from one wallet does not multiply voting power; splitting stake only divides it. To fake broad support, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying market cost and losing access to that capital. The fable of free identities meets an ivory gate, while the vine of Sybils grows only as far as the attacker’s stake.
